svg.title: Architect MUD architecture flowchart
svg.desc: Three clients — the player client, the dev panel, and the Studio and Modelshop authoring tools — reach the server two ways: a raw WebSocket carries all gameplay in both directions, while HTTP REST carries content editing only, and the two never cross. A player command enters handleCommand and passes through five dispatch stages in order: SIFT target resolution, input matchers, plugin commands, specialized actions, and finally engine builtins; the first match wins, so plugins beat builtins. Handlers reach each other through four seams — actions, hooks, events and registries — across 137 plugins. Everything mutates the world Maps, an in-memory hub in server slash engine slash world dot js that is authoritative at runtime and that every hot path reads instead of querying. From the hub, fields are written to PostgreSQL by tier: durable fields write through immediately, checkpoint fields set a dirty flag and are flushed in one batched statement, and derived fields are never written and are rebuilt at boot. Below Postgres, world content lives as 41,495 JSON files in git; a push to main is the deploy, and CI backs up production, applies the schema, imports the content and gates on the regression suite. Postgres then boot-loads back into the world Maps, and room output broadcasts from the hub back out to zone occupants over the WebSocket, closing the loop.
svg.text: CLIENTS — VANILLA JS, NO BUILD STEP
what you edit is what runs
no one touches code to author
with no DB in the process
so there is no second preview
ws · permessage-deflate · all gameplay, both ways
→ command · move · say · attack · buy · instrument_note
one look was 34 KB uncompressed; it is 1.7 KB on the wire now
▸ No REST for gameplay. No WebSocket for content editing. The two surfaces never cross — which is what lets the dev panel exist without being a second game server.
server/engine/commands/index.js — the order below IS the architecture
▸ Stage 3 precedes stage 5, so an engine builtin whose verb a plugin has claimed is dead code that still looks alive.
This is the first thing to check before editing any command handler.
SEAMS & PLUGINS — HOW CODE REACHES CODE WITHOUT IMPORTING IT
197 sites · dispatched BY NAME, so demolition
charges a crime without importing surveillance
gather from everyone, OR last-non-undefined wins
one quests subscriber yields a whole objective type
47 move gates · 45 status effects · 23 lock types
combat · survival · crime · surveillance · jail · stealth
42 of them declare no verbs at all — pure hook subscribers,
adding behaviour to flows they never expose a command for
126 ship their own regress.js — 37,785 lines, none loads in prod
zones · npcs · doors · furniture · orgs · players · spawnTimers · flags
Authoritative at runtime. Every hot path — per move, per swing, per tick — reads here and never queries.
A cache is only as safe as its write funnel: furniture (~40 scattered writers) and npcs had to earn theirs through
three helpers each before they were allowed to live here. Bulk writers re-cache exactly the rows Postgres returns.
PERSISTENCE TIERS — PICK ONE BEFORE WRITING THE CODE
one round trip for every dirty player
149 tables · one query() helper · NO ORM
SCHEMA_SQL is 3,234 lines of idempotent DDL in ONE file. Nothing migrates on boot — schema and content are deliberate acts.
Remote. Every query() is a pool checkout plus a network round trip, so the cost that matters is round-trip COUNT, never query complexity.
CONTENT — THE CODEX PIPELINE, FLOWING UP
one file per entity, all in git
no separate publish step, and no
world content anywhere in the code
a red suite stops the deploy
The import is an upsert that replaces whole columns, so editing a file is enough to REMOVE a key — which is why a one-shot script against prod is needed far less often than it looks.
